summary: Totsudo Kato (1870-1949) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Oriental Hall, Kyoto Horitsu Gakko, and Chuo University under Seiran Ouchi, Enryo Inoue, and Bankon Shimada, later teaching at Shakutoku Kyoko, Setagaya Gakuen, Komazawa, Toyo, and Nihon universities.

Touhoi Fok (1940-2018) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He studied at the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, and Otani University, later serving as a lecturer at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~1972-1986).

Touraj Daryaee (born 1967) specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history. He studied at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1991-1999) and held a post at the University of California, Irvine (~2007).

Towao Sakaehara (born 1946) is a historian and Japanologist who earned his doctoral degrees at Kyoto University. He taught at Otemon Gakuin University (1975) and Osaka City University (1981-2010), and later served as director of the Osaka Museum of History (2014-2020).

Traian Costa (1926-1995) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Vlad Bănăȓeanu (~1945-1949) and served as a professor at the University of Bucharest, where he taught Sanskrit in 1963.

Trang T. D. Nguyen works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Ho Chi Minh City Open University, University of Nebraska-Lincoln, University of South Wales, and the University of Vienna, and held posts with Play for Peace, Fuji Xerox Vietnam, and ENV.

Travis L. Smith specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at UC Berkeley and Columbia University (PhD 2007) under John Stratton Hawley, Vasudha Dalmia, Robert P. Goldman, and Sally J. Sutherland Goldman, and held posts at Barnard, Florida, and Berkeley.
Trent Walker is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Alexander von Rospatt.

Trevor Leggett (1914-2000) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Indology. He studied at King's College London, SOAS, and under Hari Prasad Shastri, Arthur Waley, and Yukio Tani. He headed the BBC Japanese Service (~1946-1970) and lectured for the Buddhist Society.

Trevor Ling (1920-1995) specialized in religious and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Oxford, he taught at the University of Nottingham, served at Judson Church in Rangoon, and held professorships at the universities of Leeds, Manchester, and Visva-Bharati.

Trijang Rinpoche (1901-1981) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Gyuto Monastery and under masters including Pabongkhapa Dechen Nyingpo and Serkong Tsenshap Rinpoche. He succeeded Ling Rinpoche and taught the 14th Dalai Lama, Kelsang Gyatso, and Loden Sherab Dagyab.

Trine Brox specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at UiT The Arctic University of Norway and the University of Copenhagen (PhD 2009) under Christian K. Wedemeyer, and became an associate professor at the University of Copenhagen in 2014.
Trinle Lhundrub studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Troy Organ (1912-1992) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Iowa (~1937-1941). He held academic posts at Parsons College, the University of Akron, Chatham University, and Ohio University.

Trulshik Rinpoche (1924-2011) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, and others, and taught prominent figures including the 14th Dalai Lama, Phakchok Rinpoche, and Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche.

Truman Michelson (1879-1938) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Harvard, Leipzig, Bonn, and Columbia under Franz Boas. He worked at the University of Missouri, George Washington University, the Bureau of American Ethnology, and the Smithsonian Institution.
Trung Huynh is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who completed his PhD at the University of the West under the supervision of Darui Long (attested 2016).

Trungram Gyaltrul Rinpoche (born 1968) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute and earned a PhD from Harvard under Leonard van der Kuijp, and founded the United Trungram Buddhist Foundation and Fellowship.

Trungram Gyalwa Rinpoche (born 1968) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Harvard (PhD 2004), later serving as a visiting scholar at Michigan and visiting professor at McGill (2016).
